To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The flow in the gap region is characterized by a complex interaction of the leakage and the free-stream flows.

the broadband perturbations measured in the gap region of the airfoil can be related to turbulent eddys generated in the leakage flow and that the unsteadiness of these eddys is the cause of the broadband noise.

the broadband perturbations in the tip clearance flow of an airfoil are related to turbulent structures and that the sound radiated in the cross-stream direction by the airfoil tip is strongly related to the unsteady pressure field measured in the gap region.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: • Identification of the aeroacoustics sources of a tip clearance flow • Influence of the gap size and the gap shape • Identification of the turbulent structures in the gap • Identification of the unsteady pressure fluctuations and their relationship to the turbulent structures in PIV and PIV measurements • Influence of the tip geometry and the airfoil shape • Influence of the angle of attack • Comparison of the results with numerical simulation.
aeroacoustic noise sources and their interaction with the surrounding turbulent flow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the unsteady tip clearance flow is the source of broadband noise.
the tip clearance flow is a very complex flow, with a large variety of unsteady phenomena, which are not only related to the tip vortex.

• the tip clearance flow is characterized by a strong unsteady broadband perturbation • the perturbations are mainly due to the interaction of the leakage jet with the main flow • the perturbatons are mainly generated in the gap • the perturbtations are mainly radiated into the wake • the perturbantions radiated into the gap are mainly radiated in the cross stream direction • the perturbants are mainly radiated at low frequency and at low Strouhal number •
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unsteady broadband pressure fluctuations are mainly generated by the turbulent flow in the gap and that these fluctuations are related to acoustic radiation.

the unsteady broadband noise generated in the gap is mainly caused by the turbulent eddies in the gap and that the acoustic radiation is mainly related to the unsteady pressure fluctuations on the airfoil surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a tip gap flow can generate broadband noise, which can be related to the turbulent flow in the gap region using a wavelet analysis.
the tip clearance flow generates broadband sound that is related to the unsteady turbulent flow in the gap region.
the gap flow, which is highly unsteady, is the main source of noise in a tip clearance configuration.
